summary: Add a simple Angular employee-management frontend to the existing EmployeeManagement project. The frontend will use the existing ASP.NET Core API at http://localhost:5273 for employee CRUD operations.

workspaceSignals.decisionReason: The workspace already contains an ASP.NET Core EmployeeManagement API with employee CRUD routes and a SQL Server-backed data layer; only a new frontend is planned.

questions.question: Which programming language for Employee Management API?
questions.rationale: The existing API project targets net10.0 and is implemented in C#.

questions.question: Which framework for Employee Management API?
questions.rationale: The existing backend uses ASP.NET Core controllers.

questions.question: Describe the features or API routes for Employee Management API.
questions.recommendedChoice: Existing employee CRUD API: GET /api/employees, GET /api/employees/{id}, POST /api/employees, PUT /api/employees/{id}, and DELETE /api/employees/{id}.
questions.answer: Existing employee CRUD API: GET /api/employees, GET /api/employees/{id}, POST /api/employees, PUT /api/employees/{id}, and DELETE /api/employees/{id}.
questions.rationale: These routes are defined in the existing EmployeesController.

questions.question: Which programming language for Employee Management Frontend?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Type-safe language commonly used with Angular

questions.rationale: Angular is requested and its standard application language is TypeScript.

questions.question: Which frontend framework for Employee Management Frontend?
questions.rationale: The user explicitly requested an Angular frontend.

questions.question: Describe the features or API routes for Employee Management Frontend.
questions.recommendedChoice: A clean, responsive employee-management UI using the existing API: browse employees, view details, and create, edit, or delete employee records. Include form validation and loading, empty, success, and error states.
questions.answer: A clean, responsive employee-management UI using the existing API: browse employees, view details, and create, edit, or delete employee records. Include form validation and loading, empty, success, and error states.
questions.rationale: The user requested an employee-management UI, and the existing API provides employee CRUD endpoints.

questions.question: Which data stores does your app need?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: The frontend uses the existing API and adds no independent persistence

questions.rationale: This augmentation is a frontend that consumes the existing API; it adds no independent data store or Azure storage service.

questions.question: Does this app need user login?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Add a user sign-in flow and authenticated API access

options.label: No
options.description: No user sign-in or authenticated API access

questions.rationale: The existing API does not expose an authentication flow, and the user did not request sign-in.
